description:
MAINTAINER DECISION, 2026-08-13: 'I need a global 0.1s timestep to be used. Have additional outer correctors to prevent the courant number problem.' Agent dispatched same day.

WHY -- pacing alone cannot reach real time. MEASURED, release mode, the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep, 20,000 steps of 1 ms:
  41.79 s quiescent / 49.00 s contended  =>  2.09-2.45 ms of COMPUTE per 1 ms of PLANT time
  old pacing (compute + 10 ms sleep per 10 ms tick): real-time ratio 0.29-0.32
  new deadline pacing (landed 2026-08-13):           0.41-0.48
Reducing SUBSTEPS_PER_TICK does NOT help -- it cuts plant time per tick in the same proportion as compute.
The physics is ~2.2x too expensive at dt = 1 ms. A longer timestep is the route; that is this bead.
The 20 percent duty figure in op-szmi.16 predates the nodalised SG (edbb2bd7) and is off by ~12x -- do not use it.

THE ASK:
1. ONE GLOBAL 0.1 s TIMESTEP. Today the step is pinned by at least THREE hand-maintained literals:
     app/mod.rs PHYSICS_DT_S
     physics/primary_loop.rs:421 STEAM_GENERATOR_SUBSTEP_S = 0.0125
     physics/primary_loop.rs:381 STEAM_GENERATOR_NODE_COUNT = 8 (interacts with it)
   Global means a single shared constant every consumer reads, not three literals that happen to agree.
2. OUTER CORRECTORS for stability. A 100x longer step will violate the Courant condition on advective paths;
   the maintainer wants PIMPLE-style iterate-to-convergence within a timestep rather than a smaller step.

SEARCH-BEFORE-BUILDING, already checked -- REUSE these:
  Courant: tuas .../fluid_mechanics_correlations/courant_number.rs;
           .../one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling/preprocessing.rs;
           .../pre_built_components/heat_transfer_entities/preprocessing/;
           TuasLibError::CourantMassFlowVectorEmpty already exists for the degenerate case.
  Correctors: tampines/src/multiphase_1d/drift_flux.rs (+ edwards_tests.rs);
              outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/ and src/io/fv_solution/ (nOuterCorrectors vocabulary);
              MOST LIKELY DIRECT REUSE per root CLAUDE.md: TampinesSteamArray and OPCPFluidArray already wrap
              fvm:: operators WITH PIMPLE correctors, and the SG already uses those arrays -- check first.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - MEASURE the Courant number per advective path at 0.1 s, before and after correctors. Do not assume it.
  - Do not silently loosen a tolerance or convergence criterion to make 0.1 s look stable.
  - V&V numbers WILL move. Re-measure, update the number AND the date, and list every one changed.
    Do not quietly edit expected values, and do not delete or ignore a test that becomes inconvenient.
  - Report the new real-time ratio from the SAME test so it is comparable to 0.41-0.48.
  - Quantify the ACCURACY trade against the 1 ms model on at least one transient. Be honest if it degrades --
    a fast simulator that is wrong is worse than a slow one that is right.

RELATED: op-v5zb (deadline pacing, landed), op-775s (the measurement, now done), op-szmi.16 (GUI frame lag --
DIFFERENT symptom, do not merge), op-xvye (P0 pacing underflow, now known to be in FOUR sites).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
DONE and PUSHED 2026-08-13 (commit 3acc9536 on develop).

Real-time ratio 0.492 -> 1.032, independently re-verified: 20 s of plant time in 19.385 s wall, isolated release run.

KEY FINDING -- the global 0.1 s timestep was NOT the win. Sweep: 1 ms 0.492, 10 ms 0.505, 100 ms 0.514. The steam
generator runs on its own clock and is ~96% of the cost, so raising the plant step bought 4%. The 2x came from the
exchanger's PIMPLE outer correctors being set to 4 when settled duty is identical at 1, 2, 3 and 4 (9.6854 MW each
against a 9.6851 MW half-substep reference). Cost is exactly linear in correctors; two of four were paid for nothing.

The timestep work still earned its keep: unifying a dozen scattered literals into PLANT_TIMESTEP_S is what EXPOSED
both the wasted correctors and a -84.5% point-kinetics error at 0.1 s (Lambda/beta = 0.154 s is comparable to the
step; fixed by sub-stepping kinetics at 1 ms). It also caught a live bug where a test window had silently doubled to
150 s and was running to 999.07 K against a 1000 K limit.

Courant measured, not assumed: Co_hot 0.222 at 0.0125 s, 1.776 at 0.1 s, hot side binding at 4.97x the cold.
Correctors provably do not lift the limit -- 0.05 s panics at 4, 8 and 16; 0.1 s at 8 and 32.

Clamp events zero everywhere, now asserted == 0 in three tests.

Accuracy: reactor power +0.0000% (STRUCTURAL -- both runs integrate kinetics at 1 ms, not a convergence result),
core outlet -0.0015 K, bed -0.054 K, SG duty -0.012%. WORSE: steam outlet +0.822 K, GUI 100 Hz -> 10 Hz.

Follow-on: op-3lay (build real buffer -- 1.032 is ~3% margin and goes negative under load).

title: htgr_sim_v1: global 0.1 s timestep with outer correctors -- the route to real time
